Getting started

Open Elastic and connect it to the robot

1

Open Elastic

Driver Station gear tab: set Dashboard Type to Elastic. Or VS Code: WPILib logo, Start Tool, Elastic.

2

Open the network settings

Click Settings, then the Network tab.

3

At a robot with the Driver Station running

Set IP Address Mode to Driver Station. This is the default.

4

Without the Driver Station, or in simulation

Team Number (10.TE.AM.2) with your Team Number, or localhost (127.0.0.1) for the simulator.

5

Check the bottom of the window

Network Tables: Connected means Elastic has reached the robot.

Connecting to your robot

CANDriveSubsystem.java

  /** Once, from the constructor: items with a widget. */

  private void publishWidgets() {

1   SmartDashboard.putData(this); // shows the running command

2   SmartDashboard.putData("Drive Out 1 s", driveOut(1.0));

  }

   

  /** Every 20 ms, on its own. Send what someone will read. */

  @Override

3 public void periodic() {

    SmartDashboard.putNumber(

4       "Battery (V)", RobotController.getBatteryVoltage());

    SmartDashboard.putNumber(

        "Left Output (%)",

        leftLeader.getAppliedOutput() * 100.0);

1

A subsystem widget

It shows the running command, so name yours with withName.

2

A command button

Click it to run the command on an enabled robot.

3

Every 20 ms

Send a few useful values. Put the rest in logs.

4

Units in the name

Battery (V) needs no explanation at a match.

6

Autonomous

An auto chooser with SendableChooser

RobotContainer.java

  private final SendableChooser<Command> chooser =

      new SendableChooser<>();

   

  private void configureAutoChooser() {

1   chooser.setDefaultOption("Do nothing", Commands.none());

    chooser.addOption("Drive 2 s", drive.driveOut(2.0));

    chooser.addOption("Drive 4 s", drive.driveOut(4.0));

2   SmartDashboard.putData("Auto", chooser);

  }

   

  /** Robot.java calls this when auto starts. */

  public Command getAutonomousCommand() {

3   return chooser.getSelected();

  }

1

A safe default

If nobody picks, the robot does nothing.

2

Send it once

Drag Auto out of SmartDashboard in Add Widget.

3

Read it late

Calling getSelected() here means the last pick wins.

7

Common mistake

Live tuning: Enter disables an enabled robot

What you see

You type a new value into a box, press Enter, and the enabled robot stops.

Why it happens

Enter is the Driver Station shortcut for Disable, even while you are typing.

The fix

Robot enabled? Click the box’s submit button: Show Submit Button in Edit Properties.

SmartDashboard.setDefaultNumber("Drive Scale", DRIVE_SCALE); // once: only fills an empty box

DoubleSupplier driveScale =

    () -> SmartDashboard.getNumber("Drive Scale", DRIVE_SCALE); // every loop: reads the box

Best practice

A clean driver tab and a noisy debug tab

Driver tab: a quick glance

Battery and the auto chooser, drawn large.

Nothing you need to read twice.

Layout locked for matches.

Debug tab: everything

Motor outputs, gains and graphs.

Subsystem widgets and command names.

Keys with units, like Left Output (%).

Deck 5 · Elastic

10

Best practice

Keep the layout on the robot

Put the layout file in your deploy folder, so it lives in the repo and on the robot.

Save keeps it inside Elastic on one laptop. Save As writes a .json file you can commit. Download From Robot gives any laptop the same layout.

// In Elastic: File, Save As, into src/main/deploy/elastic-layout.json. Then deploy.

// Elastic's Download From Robot looks on port 5800, so start this once at startup.

private void serveLayout() {

  WebServer.start(5800, Filesystem.getDeployDirectory().getPath());

}

Elastic extras

Driver notifications and tab switching

RobotContainer.java

1 private final Elastic.Notification warning =

      new Elastic.Notification(

2         Elastic.NotificationLevel.WARNING,

          "Low battery",

          "Swap it.");

   

  private void configureDriverAlerts() {

    new Trigger(this::batteryLow)

3       .debounce(LOW_BATTERY_SECONDS)

        .onTrue(once(() -> Elastic.sendNotification(warning)));

    RobotModeTriggers.autonomous()

4       .onTrue(once(() -> Elastic.selectTab("Autonomous")));

    RobotModeTriggers.teleop()

4       .onTrue(once(() -> Elastic.selectTab("Teleoperated")));

  }

1

Copy the helper

Add Elastic.java from Elastic’s repo to your util folder.

2

A popup

A level, a title and text. It shows for 3 s by default.

3

Wait a moment

The battery must stay low for 2 s, so a quick dip is ignored.

4

Switch tabs

selectTab takes a tab name. No match means no change.

12

Common mistake

Six symptoms and where they come from

What you seeWhyFix
A typed value snaps back at onceputNumber in periodic writes over the box every 20 mssetDefaultNumber once, then getNumber
A typed value is gone after a code restartNetworkTables starts empty and Elastic does not re-send itCopy good values into Constants.java
A widget is blankAn old layout: the key was renamed, or never sentRemove it and drag in the new key
A number never changesThe code sent it once, from a constructorSend it from periodic
Every widget looks dimmedElastic is disconnectedRead the bottom bar, then IP Address Mode
The chooser shows a red markThe robot lacks your pick. In 2026.1.1, Show As on a chooser stops it sendingLeave it as ComboBox Chooser

13

Exercise

Build a driver tab and save it

1.

Add the Battery (V), Left Output (%) and Auto code, then deploy or simulate.

2.

Click Add Widget, expand SmartDashboard, and drag Battery (V) and Auto to Teleoperated.

3.

Right-click Battery (V), then Show As, Voltage View.

4.

Click +, rename the new tab Debug, and drag Left Output (%) onto it.

5.

File, Save As, into src/main/deploy/elastic-layout.json.

Done when: Auto shows a green check, and the file is in your deploy folder.
